newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end sharply off on Fla crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end sharply off on Fla crop estimate.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed the daily limit lower in the back months and sharply down in the benchmark September contract after a private estimate of the 1997/98 Florida crop filtered into the market.
Mixed selling pressured the spot month to a new contract low of 69.50 cents before it closed down 9.60 at 69.65 cents. The daily limit for the spot contract is 10.00 cents.
The rest of the board settled the daily 5.00-cent limit lower for the deferred months.
Benchmark September fell to its lowest level since trading at a monthly average of 69.10 cents in February 1993, analysts said.
"Now is the time to take your equity profits and go long orange juice," Philip Lesser, an economist with the Florida Department of Citrus, said.

While Citrus Consulting International refused to release its number to the public, industry sources said the forecast came in at a record 253.0-253.5 million 90-lb boxes. Expectations ranged from 230-235 million boxes.
"We do not comment on our estimates," a spokeswoman with Citrus Consulting International, said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its estimate of the 1997/98 crop in October. The current crop was pegged at a record 225.7 million boxes.

Players said the private estimate is a barometer for price movement over the next year. The firm's ability to forecast the crop to within 5 percent of the USDA's final estimate has strengthened its reputation within the industry, sources said.
"People believe what she says is truth," a juice trader said in reference to the firm's president, Elizabeth Steger.
"She's trained at this and she does it methodically," Lesser of the Department of Citrus said, adding that Steger's clients allow her to survey their groves and count each tree limb.
Prices are likely to ease further on Friday but trade selling could support prices around 69.00 cents, dealers said.
An estimated 13,000 lots changed hands compared with Wednesday's official 2,815 lots.
